text:
Dear Ms. Karlsson,

I am delighted to confirm that the Board of Trustees has approved your nomination as a member of the Advisory Council of the Linden Arts Foundation. The Council meets four times a year, and members are expected to attend at least three meetings annually. [1] Your term will run for three years, after which you will be eligible for reappointment for a second term.

Although the position is unremunerated, the Foundation will [2] reasonable travel expenses on production of receipts. [3] a member is unable to attend a meeting, apologies should be sent to the secretary at least forty-eight hours beforehand. Members are also asked to declare any interest that might [4] with their duties.

Yours sincerely,
Olivier Bastien
Chair of Trustees

choices: Your experience in the museum sector will be particularly valuable as the Foundation reviews its acquisitions policy.
Your experience in the museum sector will be particularly valued by the staff who reviewed your acquisitions application.
Your experience in the museum sector would be particularly valuable if the Foundation had reviewed its policy last year.
Your absence from the museum sector will be particularly regretted as the Foundation reviews its acquisitions policy.
questions.explanation: The next sentence sets out the length of the term, so the previous sentence should explain the invitation positively; only the first does so coherently. The others refer to an application, use a hypothetical past, or regret an absence.
A foundation 'reimburses' expenses, meaning repays them; 'reinforce', 'reinstate' and 'reiterate' do not take 'expenses' sensibly.
'In the event that a member is unable to attend' introduces a possible situation; 'inasmuch as' would give a reason, and the others express concession.
An interest that might 'conflict with' duties is the fixed collocation; 'confront' takes no 'with', 'confine' means restrict, and 'confess' means admit.

text:
Retailers Wrestle With the Cost of Returns

Online retailers are discovering that the convenience they offer customers has a price. Around a fifth of goods bought on the internet are returned, [1] the proportion in physical stores is closer to one in twenty. The expense of collecting, inspecting and restocking these items now weighs heavily on margins.

[2] Several fashion chains have begun to charge customers for returns, a step that was unthinkable only two years ago. Others are experimenting with so-called returnless refunds, [3] shoppers are allowed to keep low-value items rather than send them back. Analysts caution that the strategy may prove [4] if it encourages customers to order more than they intend to keep.

questions.explanation: 'Whereas the proportion in physical stores is closer to one in twenty' contrasts online and store returns; the others do not express contrast.

choices: The financial pressure has encouraged companies to extend policies that, until recently, were treated as a competitive disadvantage.
The financial pressure has forced companies to reconsider policies that, until recently, were treated as a competitive advantage.
The financial pressure has forced customers to reconsider policies that, until recently, were treated as a company secret.
The financial pressure had forced companies to reconsider policies that, until recently, would have been treated as an advantage.
questions.explanation: The next sentence reports chains starting to charge for returns, which reverses a previously generous policy; only the first option introduces that reversal. The others describe extension, shift the subject to customers, or use an unsuitable past perfect.
'Whereby shoppers are allowed to keep low-value items' defines how the refund scheme works (by which); 'whereas' contrasts, 'wherein' means in which, and 'whereupon' means after which.
A strategy that encourages over-ordering would be 'counterproductive', defeating its own purpose; the others do not fit.

text:
Valmont Technical Institute – Admissions Requirements

Applicants for the Higher Diploma in Mechanical Engineering must hold either a recognized upper-secondary qualification or equivalent professional experience. [1] Those who do not meet the standard entry criteria may nevertheless be considered, [2] they can demonstrate relevant achievement through a portfolio of work.

All applicants are required to submit two references, at least one of which should be from a [3] employer or teacher. [4] we receive a large number of applications each year, interviews are offered only to those whose submissions meet the published criteria.

choices: Proficiency in mathematics is regarded as essential, and a grade equivalent to a B is normally expected in that subject.
Proficiency in mathematics is regarded as optional, and a grade equivalent to a D is normally accepted in that subject.
Proficiency in literature is regarded as essential, and a grade equivalent to a B is normally expected in that subject.
Proficiency in mathematics was regarded as essential, and a grade equivalent to a B had normally been expected.
questions.explanation: The following sentence refers to those who 'do not meet the standard entry criteria', so the previous one must state a criterion; the first does. The others make mathematics optional, name another subject, or use a past perfect.
'Provided that they can demonstrate relevant achievement' sets the condition for considering them; the others do not.
A 'former employer' is a previous one; 'forward', 'formal' and 'formidable' do not fit.
'Because we receive a large number of applications' gives the reason for restricting interviews; the others do not fit.
